session.question: In the context of OSC, what does the systematic review say about its environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, and why is it considered timely to identify the factors that advanced and enhanced its environmental performance in developed and developing regions?
session.answer:
The systematic review reports that off-site construction (OSC) has been shown to improve environmental performance, particularly by reducing waste generation and carbon emissions. However, despite these documented benefits, OSC adoption remained limited, and by 2018 no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

The review argues that this gap between strong environmental evidence and low market uptake makes it timely to identify the factors that have advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance in both developed and developing regions. Comparing these regions is intended to clarify differences, similarities, and critical success factors that can support broader adoption and improved sustainability outcomes. (jayawardana2023environmentalsustainabilityof chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-4659fb95: The review states that off-site construction (OSC) has been shown to improve environmental performance, especially by reducing waste generation and carbon emissions. Despite these well-documented benefits, OSC adoption remained limited; by 2018, no major market had exceeded 20% OSC penetration. Because of this gap between proven environmental advantages and relatively low market uptake, the authors argue it is timely to identify the factors that have advanced and enhanced OSC’s environmental performance, particularly by comparing lessons and strategies from developed and developing regions. This can help explain differences, similarities, and critical success factors for broader adoption and better sustainability outcomes.
From Janappriya Jayawardana, Asela K. Kulatunga, J. A. S. C. Jayasinghe, Malindu Sandanayake, and Guomin Zhang. Environmental sustainability of off-site construction in developed and developing regions: a systematic review. Journal of Architectural Engineering, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1061/jaeied.aeeng-1420, doi:10.1061/jaeied.aeeng-1420.

pqac-8b4b8d59: The excerpt provides the bibliographic details and abstract of a 2021 systematic review on global value chains (GVCs) and the environmental sustainability of emerging market firms. It says the literature is fragmented, and that GVCs play a dual and multilayered role in firms’ environmental sustainability. The abstract emphasizes that emerging market firms’ strategies, capabilities, and collaborative GVC relationships are important for implementing environmental practices. However, it does not mention OSC, OSC’s environmental performance, its market penetration by 2018, or reasons related to identifying factors behind its environmental performance in developed and developing regions.
From İsmail Gölgeci̇, Dilshod Makhmadshoev, and Mehmet Demirbağ. Global value chains and the environmental sustainability of emerging market firms: a systematic review of literature and research agenda. International Business Review, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ibusrev.2021.101857, doi:10.1016/j.ibusrev.2021.101857.

pqac-e09b4151: The excerpt is about firms’ ESG performance in emerging versus developed countries. It says that in emerging environments, the country effect prevails and the board of directors has a positive effect, while in developed countries the board of directors is the main mechanism influencing ESG performance and ownership also matters. However, it does not mention OSC, OSC’s environmental performance, market penetration by 2018, or any timing/region-specific reasons for identifying factors that improved OSC’s environmental performance.
From María Belén Lozano and Jennifer Martínez‐Ferrero. Do emerging and developed countries differ in terms of sustainable performance? analysis of board, ownership and country-level factors. Research in International Business and Finance, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ribaf.2022.101688, doi:10.1016/j.ribaf.2022.101688.

pqac-ed6d4341: This excerpt is about vertical green structures (VGS), not OSC. It describes VGS as a nature-based solution for buildings that can provide ecosystem services such as air purification, biodiversity enhancement, and noise reduction. The paper reviews market development, taxonomy, and environmental/economic features of VGS products, aiming to assess sustainability and guide product selection. It does not mention OSC, its environmental performance, market penetration by 2018, or factors affecting its performance in different regions.
From Ozge Ogut, Nerantzia Julia Tzortzi, and Chiara Bertolin. Vertical green structures to establish sustainable built environment: a systematic market review. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su141912349, doi:10.3390/su141912349.
